- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 81.20 → 83.25), then corrects with a lagged downward bias.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of forecast, suggesting mean reversion toward recent low/high trends.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (10+ days) — exhibits horizon-dependent bias.
- When history shows a strong upward trend, model fails to fully capture the momentum, underestimating the peak.
- When history shows a strong downward trend, model overestimates the decline, missing the bottom.
- Model exhibits “lagged correction” — true values often exceed forecasts by 1–2 days, suggesting a delay in adjusting to new information.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent high values — if last 5 days are high, model tends to overpredict, then corrects later.
- Model underestimates when true values are above 80.00, especially if preceded by a spike — exhibits “spike suppression” bias.
- Forecasts are more accurate when history is stable or trending slowly — less error when volatility is low.
